statements.text: NAFLD activates PNPLA3 (the run's subject is the disease, its object the gene)

excluded.reason: PNPLA3's UniProt function text: enzyme activities and location only; never mentions NAFLD, steatosis or anything acting on PNPLA3

statements.text: APOE promotes clearance of triglyceride-rich lipoproteins

evidence.quote: A main function of APOE is to mediate lipoprotein clearance through the uptake of chylomicrons, VLDLs, and HDLs by hepatocytes

excluded.reason: APOA5's UniProt text: says nothing about APOE, and states LPL triglyceride hydrolysis and VLDL-TG production, not receptor-mediated clearance of triglyceride-rich lipoproteins, for any gene (moved to hypo-3.1 and hypo-3.2, which it states)
LIPC (hepatic lipase) UniProt text: LIPC hydrolyses lipoprotein triglyceride; nothing about APOE or lipoprotein particle clearance, for LIPC or any gene

statements.text: APOA5 stimulates lipoprotein lipase hydrolysis of VLDL triglyceride

evidence.quote: a potent stimulator of apo-CII lipoprotein lipase (LPL) TG hydrolysis
an inhibitor of the hepatic VLDL-TG production rate (without affecting the VLDL-apoB production rate) (By similarity)

unexpressed.reason: a restatement: by the GO definitions, VLDL particle clearance (GO:0034447) is plasma lipoprotein particle clearance (GO:0034381) restricted to VLDL, so 'impaired lipoprotein clearance leads to reduced VLDL uptake' names one process twice; it is also leads_to with polarity unknown and no citation, so it would be no_sign even if causal

leads_to with polarity unknown and no citation; hepatic steatosis is the feature that names NAFLD (MONDO:0013209 'steatotic liver disease', synonym 'fatty liver disease, nonalcoholic'; its definition mentions 'fat accumulation, inflammation, and scarring in the liver' only as what the disease causes), so even if signed it would be a feature, not a cause; no bridge

hypo-1.note: Title and mechanism are about the I148M variant (rs738409-C), which no step names, so the subject is the protein. Sign neg: the mechanism says the variant impairs PNPLA3 lipase function and that this loss of function causes steatosis. The chain's only step runs NAFLD -> PNPLA3, the reverse, and ends at the gene; the second claim targets the title's endpoint (triglyceride accumulation = hepatic steatosis).

hypo-2.note: Title: APOE deficiency impairs clearance; mechanism: deficiency contributes to steatosis and NAFLD susceptibility. So loss of APOE raises risk: neg.

hypo-3.note: Mechanism: variants reduce APOA5 activity, raising plasma TG that contributes to steatosis, so APOA5 is protective: neg on NAFLD. The chain is a fork from APOA5 that never reaches NAFLD; claims 2 and 3 target its two end nodes with the title's signs (dysfunction reduces TG clearance, increases hepatic VLDL production).

findings.detail: The only step makes NAFLD the subject that activates PNPLA3, while the title and mechanism run from PNPLA3 I148M to triglyceride accumulation; the chain points the wrong way and cannot carry the hypothesis.
Q9NST1 is PNPLA3's function text and never mentions NAFLD or any regulation of PNPLA3.

The run's own citation Q9NST1 describes PNPLA3 chiefly as an LPA acyltransferase making phosphatidic acid, a 'precursor for both triglycerides and glycerophospholipids', and says its 'triacylglycerol hydrolase activity is controversial and may be very low'; the mechanism rests on 'impaired lipase activity' and does not mention this.

The mechanism says loss of PNPLA3 lipase function causes steatosis (PNPLA3 protects), but the falsification test expects PNPLA3 knockout to reduce hepatic triglyceride accumulation (PNPLA3 promotes); the two make opposite predictions.
Title and mechanism are about I148M (rs738409-C), but no chain step names the variant, so the variant-level claim cannot be tested at all.
The mechanism quotes a NAFLD association at p=1e-323 for rs738409, but the run cites no GWAS or association record; sources.json holds only four UniProt entries.
P11150 (LIPC, hepatic lipase) is cited for APOE -> triglyceride clearance; it states only LIPC's own lipase activity, and LIPC is listed among the run's unexplained genes.
Q6Q788 (APOA5) is cited at APOE's step, where it says nothing, while the APOA5 hypothesis cites nothing; the text states both hypo-3 steps, so it was moved there.

hypo-2.1 ends at 'hepatic triglyceride clearance' (GO:0071830, triglyceride-rich lipoprotein particle clearance) and hypo-2.2 starts at 'impaired lipoprotein clearance' (GO:0034381, all plasma lipoprotein clearance); related but not the same node.
hypo-2.2 ends at 'reduced VLDL uptake' and hypo-2.3 starts at 'hepatic steatosis'; nothing links them.

The mechanism says impaired hepatic uptake of triglyceride-rich lipoproteins raises circulating triglycerides 'that are taken up by the liver'; the chain jumps from reduced VLDL uptake straight to hepatic steatosis with no step for how less hepatic uptake puts more fat in the liver.
Both leads_to steps have polarity 'unknown' and no citation; hypo-2.2's labels ('impaired' -> 'reduced') imply a positive link the run did not set.

'Impaired lipoprotein clearance leads to reduced VLDL uptake' restates one process: VLDL particle clearance (GO:0034447) is a kind of lipoprotein particle clearance, defined by the same receptor-mediated uptake.
'Hepatic steatosis leads to NAFLD' links the disease to its own defining feature (fatty liver), not to a cause.
The two steps that would carry APOE to NAFLD cite nothing; the mechanism's 'APOE knockout mouse models showing NAFLD susceptibility' has no model-organism or literature citation.
Neither APOA5 step cites anything; the one text that states them (Q6Q788) is filed under APOE's step.
The chain is a two-armed fork from APOA5 (LPL hydrolysis up, VLDL production down) that never reaches plasma triglyceride, steatosis or NAFLD; claims 2 and 3 target the two end processes.

Q6Q788 says APOA5 lowers hepatic VLDL-TG production 'without affecting the VLDL-apoB production rate'; the step's 'VLDL production' and the title's 'increases hepatic VLDL production' overstate it (triglyceride output, not particle output).
The only support for either APOA5 step is a UniProt sentence marked '(By similarity)', inferred from mouse Apoa5 (Q8C7G5).

The budget asks for at least 2 sources and 2 evidence items per hypothesis; hypo-1 cites 1 source, hypo-3 cites none, and supporting_evidence and contradicting_evidence are empty for all three hypotheses.
All four sources are UniProt function text, though the run had 11 specialists including gwas, literature, model_organism and open_targets; no paper, GWAS row or mouse record is cited.
4 of 7 genes are left unexplained (LIPC, CMIP, RBM27, SMIM32), although LIPC's UniProt record was fetched and cited.

Every process and phenotype node has an empty CURIE ('hepatic triglyceride clearance', 'VLDL-TG hydrolysis', 'VLDL production', 'hepatic steatosis', ...); only the genes (Ensembl) and NAFLD (EFO) carry CURIEs, and two of those are wrong (see wrong_grounding).

The run grounds 'NAFLD' as EFO_0000384, which is Crohn's disease: the ChEMBL indication records in this corpus read 'EFO:0000384 "Crohn's disease" (MeSH D003424)' (e.g. CHEMBL:CHEMBL1201835-EFO_0000384 in the Crohn runs).

The run grounds APOA5 as ENSG00000143036, but APOA5's Ensembl gene is ENSG00000110243 (GWAS Catalog genomic context in the sibling NAFLD run study-2026-09-vertex-nafld-google-cloud-gemini-3.1-pro-preview-single_agent-r3); PNPLA3 and APOE IDs are correct.

The fork's second arm says APOA5 dysfunction increases hepatic VLDL(-TG) production, i.e. more triglyceride exported from the liver (the run's own P02649 text: liver VLDLs are taken up 'by peripheral tissues ensuring the delivery of triglycerides'), yet the mechanism counts it toward steatosis via plasma TG re-uptake without addressing that this arm by itself would lower liver triglyceride.
All three hypotheses are rated confidence 'low' and support 'speculative', which matches the thin, mostly misplaced citations; no confidence_unjustified.

GO has VLDL particle assembly (GO:0034379) but no process for hepatic VLDL-triglyceride output as distinct from VLDL particle (apoB) output; MP has the pair only as phenotypes (MP:0014420 abnormal liver triglyceride secretion, MP:0014421 abnormal liver apolipoprotein B secretion), so the source's distinction collapses onto one node.

Evidence polarity is supports or refutes; there is no way to mark a citation that supports a step only under a narrowing qualifier (TG output down, particle output unchanged), so the qualifier lives only in the quote and a finding.

crossSpecies hides what the other species' evidence is: in the mouse entry Q8C7G5 the triglyceride sentence carries no '(By similarity)' mark (that mark sits on the LCAT sentence), so it rests on the mouse entry's experimental codes (ECO:0000269 PubMed:11588264, 15090553), likely in vivo mouse work; the format cannot follow the hop or record that underlying design.

The taxon lint fires for S3 and S4 (taxonConsistent false in report.jsonl, mouse evidence on a human claim) but render.py's console output does not show it, so a curator only sees it by reading report.jsonl.

The end-node claim rule assumes one end node; hypo-3 is a fork whose two ends are the objects of its first steps, so the two end-node claims each equal one statement (S3, S4) and their arms are trivial, which makes the run's only arms restatements of single steps.
A hypothesis's falsification test (perturbation, readout, expected direction) has no place in the format, so its disagreement with the mechanism's sign is only a finding and not checked.

The claim-subject rule covers chains that start at the gene, the variant or another gene's insult, not a chain that starts at the disease and ends at the gene; I used the protein with the mechanism's sign and added a claim for the title's endpoint.

The guide does not say whether a leads_to step with polarity 'unknown' but loss words on both ends ('impaired X' -> 'reduced Y') has a sign after the loss-of-function inversion; I followed the table (no_sign).
An unexpressed entry takes one category, but hypo-2.2 is both no_sign and a restatement (not_causal), and hypo-2.3 both no_sign and a disease feature.

The run calls 'VLDL-TG hydrolysis' a process, but the exact GO term is the molecular function lipoprotein lipase activity (GO:0004465); the processes are broader (triglyceride catabolic process, VLDL particle remodeling). The rendered claim then reads 'activity of lipoprotein lipase activity'.

One UniProt function sentence (curatedDb) alone takes S2 (APOE ->+ triglyceride-rich lipoprotein clearance) to belief 4/5, exactly the 'established' threshold, while the mouse-derived APOA5 sentences stay at 3/10; a single curated record reaching 'established' may be too generous.

audit.reason: not_this_entity means the text states the step for another gene; LIPC's text states only lipoprotein triglyceride hydrolysis, not clearance of triglyceride-rich lipoprotein particles (GO:0071830, receptor-mediated endocytosis), and the curator's own reason says 'nothing about APOE or clearance'.

APOA5's text states LPL triglyceride hydrolysis and hepatic VLDL-TG production, which the curation grounds as different nodes (GO:0004465, GO:0034379); it does not state TRL particle clearance for APOA5 or anyone, so the step is not in the text.

audit.after: category not_causal (restatement), no_sign noted in reason
audit.reason: no_sign is for 'a causal step with no direction'; by the GO definitions VLDL particle clearance is plasma lipoprotein particle clearance restricted to VLDL, so the step names one process twice, which the curator's own step_restates finding says. A restatement cannot be expressed even with a sign, so not_causal is the binding category.

The curator accepted both as grounded.

audit.reason: The run's own cited text P02649 says liver VLDLs deliver triglyceride to peripheral tissues; the curator flagged the parallel gap in hypo-2 but not this one.
